cands.name: Brian Turner
cands.bio: Democrat representing North Carolina House District 116 (western Buncombe County), serving 2015–2023 and again since 2025. Grew up in Asheville. Former MTV television producer, family manufacturing company executive and UNC Asheville assistant vice chancellor. Joined Audubon North Carolina as policy director in 2023.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina endorsed Turner in the 2026 election, per Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace. We found no documented actions in his current term on data centers, homestead property taxes, land purchases by investors or foreign buyers, growth and land protection, immigration enforcement, policing, gun laws, abortion or school choice. His campaign site credits him with helping secure Pisgah View State Park and says he voted against HB2, but we found no independent record of either, so we left them out. We found no public statements from him on data centers or on more development. We found no controversies. Ballotpedia says he did not complete its candidate surveys, and its list of bills he sponsored was empty on the page we read.

local.label: Roots 90: Ballotpedia and his campaign site say he grew up in Asheville and returned to North Carolina in 2004; his birthplace is not stated on the pages reviewed.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Four terms in the NC House (2015–2023, then elected again in 2024) with seats on Appropriations committees. Earlier jobs: MTV television producer, leadership team of the family manufacturing company, UNC Asheville Director of Corporate and Foundation Relations and then Assistant Vice Chancellor. Audubon North Carolina policy director from 2023, per Wikipedia. Holds an economics degree and an MBA.
qual.why: Prior legislative service across several sessions, plus business management and policy work, fits the high band for writing law and the state budget.
